meta.title: Sunrise: Minecraft Rust Edition, Java 26.3 rewritten in Rust
meta.description: Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 rewritten in Rust. Free, open source and tested against vanilla. Get the Sunrise launcher for Windows, macOS and Linux.

footer.disclaimer: Not an official Minecraft product. Not approved by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft.
footer.who: Sunrise is made by its team: Umut, Xmilon, Juan Luci and Ari, with <team>everyone who contributes</team>. It builds on <horizon>Horizon</horizon> by Ludovic Marie and the horizon-rust contributors, and this site grew out of Horizon's, by Anthony S of <dezerx>DezerX</dezerx>. Reach us on <github>GitHub</github>. Sunrise contains no Minecraft code, assets or data, and this site offers no game files: you need your own legally obtained copy of Minecraft: Java Edition. Minecraft is a trademark of Mojang Synergies AB.
footer.licences: Sunrise's code is under the <mit>MIT licence</mit>, as Horizon's. The fonts are Geist, Geist Mono and Bricolage Grotesque, under the <ofl>SIL Open Font License</ofl>. Every asset on this site is listed in LEGAL.md.
footer.privacy: This site sets no cookies for visitors and has no analytics or trackers. Opening a release stores a keyed hash of your IP address, and sharing a performance capture stores the file you upload; downloads come from GitHub, under <github>GitHub's privacy statement</github>. The launcher sends nothing unless you allow it: <telemetry>what it can send, and how to delete it</telemetry>.
footer.madeInRust: Made in the open, in Rust.

parity.title: Where the project started.
parity.lead: Below is the project's first audit of each subsystem: what its harnesses compared then, and how much of it they covered. It is not a parity claim: players still find differences, and parity work on 26.3 continues, redstone first.
parity.audited: Audited <date/><dot/>players still find differences: <link>the open reports</link>

scale.1: its harnesses cover it and pass

loop.name: Window, input and game loop
loop.detail: The game loop, options, camera, auto-jump, toggle sprint/sneak, local input and the frame limiter match vanilla.

assets.name: Assets and resources
assets.detail: Item models match vanilla over 196,290 stacks and the client draws every item through them; the resource pack screen matches vanilla's drawing over 3,000 sessions of clicks, scrolling and searching, its incompatibility confirmation included.

network.name: Network protocol and multiplayer
network.detail: Joins vanilla servers; the dedicated server (--dedicated) matches vanilla's files, status ping, login, configuration, play, chunks, chat, recipes, advancements and command tree, a client built from vanilla's packet code joins it, Sunrise joins a vanilla server, and LAN discovery matches over 462 cases (offline mode only).

chunks.name: Chunk storage and palettes
chunks.detail: Client and saves share paletted containers, identical to vanilla over 266 scenarios.

meshing.name: Section meshing
meshing.detail: 112 scenes and over a million quads identical to vanilla.

rendering.name: Rendering
rendering.detail: Entity models, block entity renderers (407 cases, End portals, gateways and the loom's banner preview included) and their animations (296 cases, End gateway beams included), the HUD overlays (2,200 states), the recipe book (600 states), the player list, subtitles and the world border match vanilla.

lighting.name: Lighting
lighting.detail: Saved and relit light matches vanilla, slabs and stairs included.

worldgen.name: World generation
worldgen.detail: 2,352 whole chunks over 225 structure sites, in all three dimensions, identical to vanilla.

saves.name: Region files and saves
saves.detail: Saves round-trip with vanilla, and worlds from 1.8 to 26.2 upgrade as vanilla's DataFixers do, superflat worlds included; old options.txt and hotbar.nbt files are upgraded too.

entities.name: Entities and physics
entities.detail: Attributes, dimensions, death loot, spawn rules, natural spawning (15,500 cases), raids and patrols (1,900 cases), spawned mobs' gear, enchantments and state (finalizeSpawn, 24,000 cases) and mob AI (92 scenarios: villager breeding and gossip, the warden, ghastlings and copper golems included) match vanilla.

inventory.name: Interaction and inventory
inventory.detail: Menu clicks match over 8,000 click sequences, the loom and the crafter included; recipe book placement (6,000 cases), its buttons (1,200), the saved book (1,500) and the loom and crafter screens (1,600) match vanilla.

menus.name: Menus, HUD and chat
menus.detail: Every command runs as vanilla (758 commands over 39,685 parsed inputs), scoreboards and teams match (81,000 operations), the player list matches over 872,000 draw calls with heads drawn from players' skins (authlib's textures, SkinManager's lookup, legacy skin conversion), and the chat matches focused and scrolled; the resource pack screen (selection over 4,000 cases, drawing and its incompatibility confirmation over 3,000 sessions) and the chat input with its command suggestions, usage lines, Tab completion and history (3,000 sessions on vanilla's client command tree) match vanilla.

audio.name: Audio
audio.detail: The sound engine, sound events, music, situational music, ambience and subtitles match vanilla.

blocks.name: Block behaviours and ticking
blocks.detail: Block updates, random ticks, redstone, dispensers (6,000 cases), crafters (4,000 crafts), block entity removal (containers spill, 4,000 cases), copper golem chest sorting and the sculk family (435 scenarios: shrieker warnings and warden summoning included) match vanilla.

meta.title: 3D artists · Sunrise
meta.description: Sunrise welcomes 3D artists to make cosmetics for its players: hats, back items, shoulder pets, trails and emotes in a blocky style. Say hello on Discord.

artists.lead: Sunrise welcomes 3D artists to make cosmetics for Sunrise players: things players wear and carry that other Sunrise players see in every world and on every server. If you like making small, blocky models, we'd like to hear from you.

make.title: What we'd make together
items: Back items, such as backpacks or rigid wings.
Small pets that ride on a player's shoulder, or companions that float beside them.
Auras and trails made of a few particles.
Emotes: short animations for the player's own model.
make.note: Cosmetics only change how a player looks, never how the game plays.

fits.title: What fits
items: Low-poly models in Minecraft's blocky style, built from a few dozen cubes, with small pixel textures (16 to 64 pixels).
Your own designs. No copies of Minecraft's mobs and items, or of anyone else's work.
Art for every age, that still reads at a distance.
No capes, or anything that hangs from the shoulders like one.
Blockbench is welcome. Animation is a plus, not a requirement.

contact.title: Get in touch
contact.body: Join Sunrise's Discord and say you're a 3D artist, with a few pieces you've made: links or pictures are fine. If you'd rather write privately, write through <link>lu4ovic.com</link>.

meta.title: FAQ · Sunrise
meta.description: Answers about Sunrise: what it is, how it differs from Horizon, whether you need Minecraft, where the source is, which mods work and how to report a bug.

faq.lead: The short answers about Sunrise, and where to read more.

items.a: Sunrise is a free, open-source rebuild of Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 in Rust. It runs as a native program and holds each piece of the game to the same inputs as the vanilla game until the outputs are identical. It is unofficial: not approved by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft.

items.q: How is it different from Horizon?
items.a: Sunrise is a community fork of <horizon>Horizon</horizon>, which the horizon-rust contributors make, and it keeps Horizon's game as its base. The fork adds compatibility layers that run Java mods (Forge first, Fabric later), support for more than one game version, a built-in profiler, no ads and no telemetry: the launcher sends nothing unless you allow it. Some of this is still in progress; <releases>Releases</releases> lists what has shipped.

items.q: Do I need to own Minecraft?
items.a: Yes. You need your own legally obtained copy of Minecraft: Java Edition. Install it with the official launcher and play 26.3 once; Sunrise builds its resources from those files on your machine. It never downloads or shares game files, and this site offers none.

items.q: Is it safe, and where is the source?
items.a: The code is open under the MIT licence and public: <source>{repo}</source>, branch {ref}. The launcher and the game download from GitHub's release pages, where you can see what you are installing. Sunrise is a young project, so treat it as you would any program you did not write, and download it only from <releases>Releases</releases>.

Content mods and native Rust mods from the <mods>Mods</mods> page work today. Running Java mods is in progress: Forge support is not finished and not every mod loads yet, and Fabric comes later. For the native mod API, <apigaps>API gaps</apigaps> shows what is covered, what is partial and what is missing.

items.q: How do I report a bug or contribute?
items.a: Open an issue on <issues>{repo}</issues>: say what you did, what you expected and what happened, and attach the game's log if you have it. For the mod API work, the <board>project board</board> tracks the open gaps.

items.q: What data does this site keep?
items.a: Almost nothing: no cookies for visitors, no analytics, no trackers and no ads. The details are on the <privacy>privacy page</privacy>.
